subject: Transportation Systems
title: Charging Infrastructure
description: A fast breakdown of Charging Infrastructure for builders.

hook.text: An electric car is useless without a charger nearby. Building the network is a chicken-and-egg problem.

buildup.text: Drivers won't buy EVs without chargers. Companies won't build chargers without enough EVs to use them.

discovery.text: Government subsidies broke the cycle. The US alone is investing $7.5 billion in public charging stations.

twist.text: Fast chargers can add 200 miles of range in 20 minutes, but installing one costs $100,000 or more.

climax.text: China has more public chargers than the rest of the world combined—over 2 million and growing fast.

punchline.text: The electric future runs on chargers, not just cars.

quiz.question: What is the chicken-and-egg problem with EV charging?
options: Drivers need chargers to buy EVs, but chargers need EVs to justify their cost
